sources.title: National report on functionality assessment of tap connections, 2024
sources.publisher: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation
claims: Survey covered 19,812 Har Ghar Jal villages, 237,608 households, 761 districts and 34 states/UTs.
Table 6 publishes separate regularity, quantity, tested-quality and minimum-of-three index percentages.
Section 4.7 explicitly says the sampling design cannot identify the same household fulfilling all three parameters; the published functionality index takes their minimum.
Table 6 household-quality assessment uses microbiological laboratory testing and on-site pH; source-water chemical testing is analysed separately in the report.
limitations: Selected Har Ghar Jal villages are not all rural villages.
Published minimum index is not the observed joint share of functional household supply.
The Table 6 household-quality percentage does not establish full BIS chemical safety, including arsenic or fluoride; source-water chemical tests are a separate sample.
Quantity and quality have different sampling units; do not combine as household intersection.
Exact original publication day is unconfirmed; URL folder date is not used as publication date.
sources.locator: PDF page 18 fact sheet; page 49 quality methods; page 52 section 4.7; page 54 (printed 38), Table 6
sources.geographicScope: 34 rural states/UTs; sample of Har Ghar Jal villages
sources.retrievalStatus: Original PDF downloaded (HTTP 200); 116 pages; cited sections extracted with pypdf

findings.title: Hebbal: reported coverage preceded completed works in the audit record
findings.finding: CAG documented incomplete works in Hebbal, Shirahatti taluk, Gadag, while the village carried Har Ghar Jal reported status. The inspection record noted the taps and pipeline were not connected.
findings.response: Government stated in May 2025 that the elevated reservoir was completed by 8 April 2025; 200 metres of pipeline and 20 FHTCs remained, with certification to follow completion and trial run.
alternativeExplanations: Reported and certified Har Ghar Jal statuses are distinct administrative stages.
Subsequent completion can resolve the observed gap; the current status was not checked.
findings.falsifier: Obtain the post-April 2025 completion record, Gram Sabha certification, trial-run report and dated household service checks; these can close or revise the historical finding.
limitations: Observation is historical and bounded to the named village; no present-day failure or individual wrongdoing is inferred.

findings.title: Kerala audit sample: connection installation did not ensure regular adequate service
findings.finding: 122 of 342 surveyed beneficiaries described absent, limited or infrequent supply. CAG also reported 2,726 of 5,318 works complete in November 2024.
findings.response: Government cited 21 lakh new taps in four years, universal metering/billing, longer gestation of larger schemes, land acquisition, inter-agency coordination and delayed fund flow; revised planning targeted the extended 2028 deadline.
alternativeExplanations: Project timing and land/road permissions can delay service without demonstrating diversion or intent.
Audit sample is not a population estimate; some observations precede the requested five-year window.
findings.falsifier: Compare scheme-wise commissioned dates, road-cutting approvals, source-yield tests, supply schedules and repeat surveys for the same households after the audit.
findings.locator: Chapter IV, section 4.1; Table 4.3 and Government responses
limitations: 122/342 is a bounded audit sample, not the statewide share of households lacking safe water.

findings.title: Karnataka audit: tender timing needs contract-level follow-up
findings.period: Tenders after 31 March 2024; Government response May 2025
findings.finding: CAG records 33 tenders worth ₹251.75 crore invited or awarded after the extended tender-award deadline of 31 March 2024.
findings.response: Government said administrative approvals were issued on time, while lack of bidder participation and repeated tender calls delayed awards. CAG replied that only 13 of the 33 tenders were recalled, so this did not fully explain the delay, and central-share eligibility remained unanswered.
alternativeExplanations: Competition and procurement procedure can delay awards independently of corruption.
Tendered value, awarded value, expenditure and commissioned output are separate measures.
findings.falsifier: Retrieve original tender IDs, corrigenda, non-participation records, award dates, authorised schedule revisions and commissioning certificates for each contract.
limitations: Audit timing observation does not prove collusion, overpayment or criminal intent.

findings.title: Do not rank universal safe water by the published minimum functionality index
findings.finding: The survey explicitly cannot identify the same household meeting quantity, regularity and quality criteria. A minimum-of-marginals index cannot be treated as an observed joint household success rate.
findings.response: The source discloses this limitation in section 4.7; the dashboard should preserve that disclosure.
alternativeExplanations: Differences from administrative connection counts follow different definitions, dates and sampling, without implying false reporting.
findings.falsifier: A valid household-linked dataset measuring all conditions at the same time and a representative design would support an actual joint measure.
limitations: No arithmetic difference between connection coverage and index is labelled fraud or service deficit.

findings.title: Trace contaminant findings to tested water points and corrective retests
findings.finding: The survey quality percentage covers microbiology and pH. WQMIS discovery can support separate arsenic/fluoride investigations, but no locality contaminant values were extracted here.
findings.response: Government describes alternative sources and interim purification for affected habitations pending permanent schemes.
alternativeExplanations: A clean test at one water point/time does not establish household exposure throughout a season.
An unavailable record means unknown, not no contamination.
findings.falsifier: Obtain geocoded lab results with sampling dates, parameter thresholds, treatment records and independent retests at source and household delivery points.
findings.locator: Survey PDF page 49; WQMIS WQ2/WQ4; July 2026 policy
limitations: No contamination claim is made for an untested locality.

findings.finding: National extraction stage is 60.63%, yet 730 assessed units are over-exploited. Irrigation, domestic and industrial uses share the groundwater budget.
findings.response: Assessment categories and local aquifer records provide finer geographic context than the national aggregate.
alternativeExplanations: Rainfall, recharge, irrigation demand and assessment-boundary changes can affect stage without identifying a single actor.
findings.falsifier: Use the same assessment-unit boundary, seasonal water-level series, recharge estimates and sectoral extraction for a locality across comparable years.
limitations: No village water shortage, crop loss or drought causation is inferred solely from national statistics.
